stories.headline: Heavy rain lashes Odisha as Cyclone Akvan weakens, flood alert continues
stories.title: Heavy rain lashes Odisha as Cyclone Akvan weakens, flood alert continues
stories.summary: Heavy rain lashes Odisha as Cyclone Akvan weakens, flood alert continues
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Officials have been directed to remain alert and continue precautionary measures as persistent rain has raised water levels in most rivers.

The Odisha government has put the water resources department on high alert and ordered round-the-clock surveillance of rivers and reservoirs after Cyclone Akvan weakened following heavy rain across the state, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
However, the water resources department said the state's major rivers remained below warning and danger levels.
The depression left by Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan moved northwards over south coastal Odisha and weakened into a distinct low-pressure area on Friday, the Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar said.
It was expected to continue moving northwards over Odisha and weaken further within six hours.
Manorama Mohanty, director of the Meteorological Centre, said rainfall had reduced significantly, though some districts were expected to continue receiving rain.
These included Balasore, Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, Jagatsinghpur, Jajpur, Puri, Khurda and Cuttack.
"Very heavy rain is likely at some places, although several areas have already received substantial rainfall," Mohanty said.
Sources in the water resources department told PTI that Balasore and Cuttack districts had received average rainfall of about 50 mm by 8.30 am on Saturday.
Bhograi in Balasore recorded the highest rainfall at 143 mm, followed by Odogaon in Nayagarh at 108 mm, Buguda in Ganjam at 102 mm and Tangi-Choudwar in Cuttack at 90 mm.
The India Meteorological Department said one place in the state had received very heavy rainfall and 13 places had recorded heavy rainfall during the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Saturday.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the Odisha government was in touch with the water resources department secretary because rain was also possible in Jharkhand.

stories.headline: Srikakulam releases 15,440 cusecs as inflows moderate after cyclone floods
stories.title: Srikakulam releases 15,440 cusecs as inflows moderate after cyclone floods
stories.summary: The district administration heaved a sigh of relief as inflows are moderate compared to inflows of nearly one lakh cusecs one month ago due to the cyclone that caused havoc in Ichchapuram and other places
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: As many as 15,440 cusecs of water from the Bahuda River were discharged downstream on Saturday (November 21, 2026) morning as inflows continued from upstream, which witnessed heavy rains for the last few days with the impact of the Akvan cyclone.

The district administration heaved a sigh of relief as inflows are moderate compared to inflows of nearly one lakh cusecs one month ago due to the cyclone that caused havoc in Ichchapuram and other places.
Irrigation officials released 3,600 cusecs from the Gotta barrage of Vamasadhara, and 3,100 cusecs of Nagavali water were discharged from Narayanpur Anicut.
Srikakulam collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar said that the situation was under control in spite temporary inundation of crops in Ichchapuram and other places.
He said that agriculture officials will visit the fields and give necessary suggestions to farmers.

stories.headline: Remnants of Cyclone Akvan to bring rain in Bengal till November 22: IMD
stories.title: Remnants of Cyclone Akvan to bring rain in Bengal till November 22: IMD
stories.summary: According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph are likely over most districts of south Bengal and a few places in north Bengal on Saturday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The remnants of severe cyclonic storm Akvan, which weakened into a low-pressure area on Saturday (November 21, 2026), will bring rain to West Bengal till November 22 morning, the IMD said.
The storm moved towards West Bengal after making landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday (November 20) morning, bringing heavy rain to south Bengal since November 19 evening.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph are likely over most districts of south Bengal and a few places in north Bengal on Saturday (November 21).
Mainly dry weather is likely to prevail across the state from November 24, with minimum temperatures expected to fall by two to three degrees Celsius, the Met department said.

With the weakening storm bringing very heavy rain over the coastal districts, the seaside tourist town of Digha in Purba Medinipur district recorded the State's highest rainfall at 176 mm in 24 hours till 8.30 a.m., according to the IMD data.
Kanthi in the same district received 105 mm rainfall during the period, while Sagar island in the other coastal district of South 24 Parganas district received 85 mm rain, it said.
Kolkata received 41 mm of rain during the same period as the Met forecast a cloudy sky with light to moderate rain for the city on Saturday (November 21).

stories.headline: India says no change in its position on IWT as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
stories.title: India says no change in its position on IWT as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 20: India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday, amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday, attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice. It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor. Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum. At his bi-weekly media briefing, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked how New Delhi viewed Malik's participation in the India-hosted forum, given that he does not hold the culture portfolio and had reportedly made comments on the IWT. "As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Jaiswal said. India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours. Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play". Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan. "India is hosting the 1st SCO Civilisation Dialogue on 20-22 November 2026, in New Delhi. This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan," the MEA said in a post on X. "Observers and Dialogue Partners of the SCO have also been invited to attend the Dialogue, which will be inaugurated this evening by the Hon’ble Prime Minister," it said. The event is being hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the MEA. The SCO was founded at a summit in Shanghai in 2001 by the presidents of Russia, China, the Kyrgyz Republic, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan became its permanent members in 2017.

stories.headline: India GDP growth projected at 7% for FY27
stories.title: India GDP growth projected at 7% for FY27
stories.summary: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.

Mumbai: India’s real GDP growth is projected at approximately 7 per cent for FY27, supported by sustained public capital expenditure, resilient domestic demand and strong services activity, according to a new Brickwork Ratings (BWR) report released on Saturday.

However, persistent inflationary pressures are expected to keep monetary policy tight, with BWR anticipating a further 25-basis-point (bps) repo rate hike in December 2026, taking the policy rate to 5.75 per cent, followed by an extended pause.
“India’s growth momentum is increasingly being supported by the strength of its domestic economy and the resilience of its services exports.
However, the external environment remains an important variable, particularly given India’s dependence on energy and other key imports,” said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings.

In the current environment, businesses with healthy balance sheets, adequate liquidity and the ability to manage input-cost volatility will be better positioned to navigate uncertainty, the report said.
For the broader economy, sustaining investment momentum while strengthening external resilience will remain important, Sharan said.
Government capital expenditure reached Rs 6.55 lakh crore in the first half of FY27, supporting infrastructure investment, the report said.
Services activity remained robust, with the Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rising to 55.8 in October and the Composite PMI reaching 56.2.
Industrial production grew 6.7 per cent in September, while manufacturing output expanded 7.6 per cent.
October Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections also rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore, reflecting festive demand and higher import-related collections.
Capital goods and electrical equipment, automobiles, IT services and export-oriented sectors are relatively better positioned, the report said.

stories.headline: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
stories.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
stories.summary: The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the distribution of 15 lakh free residential sites to landless families and construction of one lakh houses during 2026-27 at an estimated cost of ₹2,241 crore.
The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19.
The initiatives aim to provide housing security to families without residential sites and those unable to afford house construction.
Under the proposed Bhooguarantee scheme of the Karnataka government, the first phase will cover five lakh sites at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore.

The government plans to develop nine lakh sites in rural areas, requiring around 45,000 acres, while five lakh urban beneficiaries will be accommodated through a G+3 housing model, according to a press release.
The government has identified 23,500 acres of government land across 31 districts, sufficient for about 4.70 lakh sites.
District administrations have been asked to identify additional land.
The first-phase development cost is estimated at ₹20,000 per site.
The proposed Niveshana Yojane will provide sites to eligible landless families, including ex-servicemen, with a 3% reservation for former defence personnel.
Priority will also be given to senior citizens, widows, divorced persons, single mothers, persons with disabilities and transgender persons.
The proposed reservation includes 19.5% for Scheduled Castes and 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes.
The Chief Minister has also directed officials to provide for reservation for Backward Classes.

stories.headline: INS Sahyadri reaches Vietnam to strengthen naval partnership
stories.title: INS Sahyadri reaches Vietnam to strengthen naval partnership
stories.summary: Hanoi, Nov 21: In a move to boost maritime cooperation between India and Vietnam, the Indian Naval Ship (INS) Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city of the Southeast Asian nation for an operational turnaround. In a post on X on Saturday, the Indian Embassy in Vietnam posted: "The ship was accorded a warm welcome by the Vietnam People's Navy and local authorities. The visit reaffirms our shared commitment to peace, stability and security in the region and in the Indo-Pacific." INS Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city on Friday for a three-day goodwill visit aimed at deepening defence ties and strengthening naval cooperation between India and Vietnam, local media reported. The Indian Navy frigate was accorded a warm welcome by local authorities, the city's armed forces and the Naval Region 3 Command. The Indian Naval ship, with 294 officers and sailors aboard, will remain in Da Nang until November 22 as part of its goodwill visit, Vietnamese newspaper SGGP reported. As part of the engagements, the Indian Navy delegation will meet the leadership of the Da Nang City People's Committee and the Naval Region 3 Command. The two navies will also participate in sports exchanges involving their officers and personnel. The crew will additionally explore the city's historical and cultural attractions. The visit is expected to promote greater mutual understanding and trust between the two naval forces and deepen defence cooperation between the two countries. Earlier this month, a four-member delegation of the Vietnam People's Army visited the College of Military Engineering (CME) in Pune, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme. The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. "Strengthening India-Vietnam Defence Cooperation. A four-member delegation of the Vietnam People's Army visited the College of Military Engineering (#CME), Pune, from 03 to 05 November 2026, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme," the Indian Army posted on X. "The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, HADR and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. The engagement further strengthened professional ties, mutual understanding and bilateral military cooperation between India and Vietnam," it added. Recently, National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval was on an official visit to Vietnam, where he called on Vietnamese President To Lam and thanked him for his 'steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership'. ( IANS)

stories.headline: Abrogation of Article 370 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth: Shah
stories.title: Abrogation of Article 370 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth: Shah
stories.summary: Itanagar, Nov 21: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said that the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth, and not a single local youth in the Valley is now involved in terrorism after 35 years of violence and unrest. He was addressing an event at Police Training Centre in Banderdewa near Itanagar in which the President's Police Colour was conferred to Arunachal Pradesh Police. "After over 35 years of violence, not a single local youth of Kashmir Valley is now involved in terrorism," he said. Recalling the troubled 90s, he said the situation in Kashmir Valley has undergone a sea change after the abrogation of Article 370. About criticism by opposition parties that the constitutional provision had no connection with terrorism, Shah said developments in the Valley have demonstrated otherwise. He said the change in the Kashmir Valley was brought about not merely by eliminating terrorists but also by ending the atmosphere of discrimination and alienation among the youth of Kashmir. Development activities undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014 had further strengthened the prospects of lasting peace, he added. Shah said the transformation in Kashmir was a matter of immense pride for the country and reflected the sacrifices and dedication of security forces and intelligence agencies. Recalling the turbulent 90s, Shah said terrorism was at its peak and there were doubts about how long the country would be able to hold on to Kashmir. "Even the chief minister of the state had left for England, while security forces, through their courage and sacrifices, ensured that the Valley remained connected with the rest of the country," he said. "Today, from this sacred land of Parshuram ji, I want to tell the entire nation with pride that the abrogation of Article 370 has brought an end to the sense of separatism among the youth of Kashmir. This is reflected in the fact that today, not a single Kashmiri youth is involved in terrorism in Kashmir Valley," he said.
